review.name: Claude Code review
review.what_it_is: Anthropic's managed PR review for Claude Code
review.verdict: Used as a PR pass alongside Codex or as a local /review skill. The recurring complaint is price, quoted at $15 to $25 per review, plus slowness and reviews that need re-checking.
review.notes: Regex caught many generic 'review' mentions; about half the snippets are false matches. Some comments conflate the managed product with the /review slash command.

review.name: Copilot code review
review.what_it_is: GitHub's built-in AI pull request reviewer
review.verdict: The low-friction pick for teams already on GitHub; several call its PR comments surprisingly insightful. Complaints center on noisy, overeager comments and the 2026 change billing reviews against Actions minutes.
review.notes: Several neutral/negative snippets come from the single thread about Actions-minutes billing.

review.name: Graphite
review.what_it_is: Stacked PR tool with AI code review
review.verdict: Mostly known for stacked PRs, with an AI review agent on top, and now part of Cursor. The one real user here credits stacks with keeping AI-era PRs small.
review.notes: 13 of 14 snippets are false matches (the mineral, Graphite monitoring, graphite.io research, a 'graphite G4'). Verdict rests on one comment plus the 'Graphite is joining Cursor' story.

review.name: CodeRabbit
review.verdict: The name people reach for when describing an AI PR reviewer, usually as the reference point. Few first-hand endorsements here; several teams say they had gripes or built their own instead.
review.notes: Three snippets are CodeRabbit staff promoting a free security deep scan. Qodo's evidence also has teams calling CodeRabbit noisy (49621594, 48407230).

review.name: Codex code review
review.what_it_is: OpenAI Codex reviewing PRs and diffs
review.verdict: Popular as the cross-vendor second opinion: write with Claude, review with Codex. Praised for catching real bugs; criticized for endless nitpick loops and an opaque separate quota.
review.notes: False matches: Slate Star Codex book review, and Codex reviewing a home server setup. One cited paper found Codex reviewing Claude drafts lowered pass rates.

review.name: Cursor Bugbot
review.verdict: The most praised review bot in these threads; users say it finds subtle bugs Claude and Codex miss. Downsides: inconsistent across rounds, and a move to per-run pricing drove some away.
review.notes: Two pairs of snippets are duplicates (same comment via ask_hn and hn_comment).

review.name: Codex Security
review.verdict: OpenAI's open-source security scanning CLI. The launch thread, answered by the Promptfoo team, is dominated by model refusals on defensive security work and slow access for open-source maintainers.
review.notes: Little first-hand usage; most snippets are vendor replies in the launch thread.

review.name: Qodo
review.what_it_is: AI code review and PR agent
review.verdict: An AI PR reviewer that teams try and often drop over noise. One user likes it for speeding up human review rather than replacing it, and Bugbot gives more quota per dollar.
review.notes: A small open-source benchmark ran Qodo/PR-Agent on an older model, so its weak score there is not conclusive.

review.name: Greptile
review.verdict: A PR review bot that shows up in several stacks next to Codex and Claude Code. One user found few false positives; others found it noisy or pricey like its rivals.
review.notes: One snippet is from Greptile's founder; another is greptile.json in PostHog's repo, showing usage but no opinion.

review.name: Open Code Review (Alibaba)
review.what_it_is: Alibaba's open-source CLI code review tool
review.verdict: Alibaba's open-sourced internal code review CLI. Commenters see the value in its curated rule files, which originally shipped in Chinese and prompted community translations; first-hand usage reports are scarce.
review.notes: Only one clear first-hand 'good experience' comment. One benchmark run was partial (4/20).

review.name: Sourcery
review.what_it_is: AI code review bot for PRs
review.verdict: A PR review bot recommended alongside CodeRabbit for catching contract violations and antipatterns. Most support comes from one repeat commenter; a team user calls it chatty but improving.
review.notes: 8 of 13 snippets are false matches (Pratchett's novel, sourceryintel.com, unrelated projects). All three positive snippets are from the same author (Leynos).

review.name: Sphinx
review.what_it_is: Hook that quizzes you on AI code
review.verdict: A Show HN hook that quizzes you on your AI's code before you ship it. The launch drew 253 points, but no user comments about it turned up.
review.notes: No evidence snippets; verdict based only on the Show HN title and points.

context.name: AGENTS.md
context.what_it_is: Open instruction file format for coding agents
context.verdict: The default home for project rules; nearly every setup described here has one, sometimes as CLAUDE.md. Pain points are files that keep growing and instructions agents still ignore.
context.notes: Several snippets are about CLAUDE.md rather than AGENTS.md; counted as the same practice. Several entries are duplicates (ask_hn and hn_comment).

context.name: Agent Skills
context.what_it_is: Open format for reusable agent instruction packs
context.verdict: Widely used for project-specific workflows and teaching agents in-house tools. A vocal minority says too many skills pollute context and that stronger models increasingly do fine without them.
context.notes: Snippets refer to skills generally, not agentskills.io specifically. Some neutral ones are resumes and job posts listing skills.

context.name: Superpowers
context.what_it_is: Skills library for structured Claude Code workflows
context.verdict: A Claude Code skills pack that walks the agent through brainstorm, design doc, plan, then build. Fans like the structure; skeptics say current models do fine run raw.
context.notes: Over half the snippets use 'superpowers' as a common word (geopolitics, 'AI gives me superpowers').

context.name: Semble
context.verdict: A code search tool for agents that claims far fewer tokens than grep. Two users keep it beside ripgrep and Serena; a skeptic says models aren't trained to use such tools.
context.notes: 15 of 21 snippets are false matches (assemble, semblance, French 'semble', the Bluesky app Semble). The author admits benchmarks are lacking.

context.name: Spec Kit
context.verdict: GitHub's spec-driven development kit, used to force requirements, plan and tasks before code. The main complaint is volume: reams of repetitive markdown that are tedious to review.
context.notes: Many neutral snippets are 'how is this different from Spec Kit' questions on competing tools.

context.name: Context7
context.what_it_is: MCP server for up-to-date library docs
context.verdict: One of the standard MCP servers people install, used to pull current library docs so the agent stops guessing APIs. No complaints turned up in these threads.

context.name: Impeccable
context.what_it_is: Design skill to de-slop AI frontends
context.verdict: A design skill for stripping the generic AI look from frontends. Users say it removes slop tells more aggressively than rivals, though output is a starting point and token use is high.
context.notes: 7 of 13 snippets use 'impeccable' as an ordinary word; the top HN story (Stratechery) is unrelated.

context.name: GitHub MCP server
context.what_it_is: Official MCP server for GitHub APIs
context.verdict: Used to let agents read issues, search dependency code and open PRs, even from ChatGPT. The open questions are whether it beats the gh CLI and how it ties into Copilot billing.

context.name: rtk
context.what_it_is: CLI proxy that compresses agent command output
context.verdict: A shell wrapper that trims command output before it reaches the agent's context. Its own stats claim big savings, but independent benchmarks found agents take more turns and save little.
context.notes: Top HN story is a critical benchmark ('RTK reports token savings, but our cost benchmarks disagree').

context.name: Graphify
context.what_it_is: Codebase knowledge graph for coding agents
context.verdict: Maps a codebase into a knowledge graph so agents spend fewer tokens. Mostly cited as the baseline rivals claim to beat; one tester found models can't use its output well.
context.notes: No first-hand reviews; most mentions are competitors' Show HN claims or resumes. Two snippets concern an unrelated graphify-csharp project.

context.name: Figma MCP
context.verdict: Turns Figma designs into code; two users credit it with faster, pixel-accurate page builds. Recent threads call it close to unusable and fault Figma for gating access to approved clients.
context.notes: Positive reports are older; recent comments (Oct-Nov 2026) are mostly negative. A Context7 snippet (46699656) also calls Figma MCP 'borderline magical'.

context.name: context-mode
context.what_it_is: Plugin that shrinks MCP output in context
context.verdict: A plugin that shrinks bulky MCP tool output before it hits the agent's context window. Only three real mentions, each from someone who keeps it in their standard setup.
context.notes: 9 of 12 snippets are false matches on phrases like 'context model'. Thin evidence.

context.name: Serena
context.what_it_is: MCP server exposing LSP code tools
context.verdict: An MCP server that gives agents language-server tools for symbol lookup, indexing and refactors. The few real users say it works well, including inside OpenCode and JetBrains IDEs.
context.notes: 6 of 13 snippets are about people named Serena; the top HN story is unrelated.

browser.name: Playwright MCP
browser.what_it_is: Microsoft's MCP server for browser automation
browser.verdict: The default way to give an agent a browser, used daily for UI checks and scraping. Works out of the box; the complaints are slowness and heavy context use.
browser.notes: Many snippets mention plain Playwright (tests, traces, resumes) rather than the MCP server; counted neutral. Top HN story is a Playwright skill pitched as lighter on context than the MCP.

browser.name: Chrome DevTools MCP
browser.what_it_is: Official MCP server for Chrome DevTools
browser.verdict: Chosen over Playwright when the agent needs real DevTools: network requests, performance traces, Lighthouse audits. Users run it for automated QA and debugging; one says it clutters context.
browser.notes: One user reports open models hallucinate its tool calls while GPT-class models are fine (49936051).

browser.name: Browser MCP
browser.what_it_is: MCP server that drives your browser
browser.verdict: Lets Cursor, Claude or VS Code drive your own browser. The Show HN drew 616 points, but later comments use 'browser MCP' generically, so there's little signal on this tool itself.
browser.notes: All 13 snippets use 'browser MCP' as a generic category; none clearly refer to browsermcp.io. 47546241 (using it to get past sites that block agent traffic) might be this tool but is ambiguous.

browser.name: agent-browser
browser.what_it_is: Vercel's browser automation CLI for agents
browser.verdict: Vercel's browser automation CLI for coding agents, often benchmarked against Playwright MCP. Users say it works fine, and its bundled skill turns up issues they would not think to test.

browser.name: browser-use
browser.what_it_is: Open-source framework for LLM web agents
browser.verdict: An open-source framework for LLM-driven web agents from YC W25, with 120k GitHub stars. Recent HN threads barely discuss it directly; it mostly appears as a benchmark comparison target.
browser.notes: 9 of 12 snippets match the generic phrase 'browser use' or 'browser user'. agent-browser can use it as a provider (49347126, in agent-browser evidence).

browser.name: Lightpanda
browser.what_it_is: Lightweight headless browser written in Zig
browser.verdict: A Zig headless browser built for agents and scraping. One team got big CPU and memory wins over Chrome; others hit pages it can't render and note it's easy to detect.
browser.notes: One site operator had to block its user agent for aggressive scraping (50080257).

browser.name: Firecrawl
browser.what_it_is: Web scraping and search API for LLMs
browser.verdict: A common scraping and search API for agents, rated well and self-hostable. Critics cite request logging, a skill that nudges agents to send feedback, and site owners paying for its customers' traffic.

browser.name: Stagehand
browser.what_it_is: AI browser automation framework by Browserbase
browser.verdict: Browserbase's open-source AI browser automation framework, with act, extract and observe calls and a cached replay layer. Threads are mostly vendor posts; one skeptic asks why not let agents write Playwright directly.
browser.notes: Most snippets are from Browserbase staff; little independent usage.

browser.name: Vibium
browser.what_it_is: Browser automation for agents from Selenium's creator
browser.verdict: Browser automation for agents from Selenium's creator, with a CLI and agent skill. Most mentions come from the creator or people watching its Claude-coauthored repo; one user wants it leaner on tokens.
browser.notes: Six of 12 snippets are by the creator (hugs / Jason Huggins).

browser.name: Claude in Chrome
browser.verdict: Used for web chores in your logged-in browser: pulling Strava GPX files, downloading Datadog logs, driving ChatGPT, validating UX. Weak spots include missed obvious errors, multi-account setups and click-hijack vulnerabilities.

browser.name: Scrapling
browser.verdict: A stealthy Python scraping library that agents call for fetching pages, often behind an MCP. One frequent user says it loads nearly any site, even Google results, though output can be context-heavy.
browser.notes: Four of six snippets are from one author (nijave). Thin evidence.

browser.name: Browserbase
browser.what_it_is: Hosted headless browser infrastructure for agents
browser.verdict: Hosted browsers for agents, from the company behind Stagehand. One startup builds on it for session persistence; site operators blame it and its peers for abusive bot traffic and captcha bypass.
browser.notes: Three snippets are Browserbase staff discussing Stagehand and their benchmark.

browser.name: Jina Reader
browser.verdict: An API that turns any URL into clean markdown for LLMs. Used as a first-pass fetcher that cuts page tokens sharply; the limit is it's read-only, with no clicking or form filling.
